title: The Mutant Prayer Thicket

features.name: the corrupted prayer-form
features.desc-on-touch: Words spiral outward in patterns that hurt to read. The prayer has learned to make its own grammar, looping endlessly into shapes no human voice could voice.

features.name: the thicket breathing
features.desc-on-touch: You stand in a tangle of growth that shouldn't exist. Branches that were never branches. The breathing you hear is the thicket learning to inhale.

features.name: prayer-dark that sees
features.desc-on-touch: A darkness in the thicket that watches. The space between words where attention still lives, even when the prayer has forgotten itself.

features.name: the mutation's edge
features.desc-on-touch: Where the prayer still sounds like prayer, and where it has already become something else. The threshold is so thin you can stand on both sides at once.

features.name: static bloom
features.desc-on-touch: Something flowering here that was never meant to flower. The bloom crackles. It is beautiful in a way that makes your teeth itch.

inscription: here the prayer learned to grow in directions that prayer should never reach

file.name: Thicket_Prayer_Corrupted_Phonemes.mp3
file.note: A recording of the prayer-field speaking. The words loop and bend. Listeners report their own prayers changing shape after hearing it.

reverie.title: REVERIE — prayer field at prayer-time
narr: You kneel in the paddock together as light turns gold.
She whispers something like a prayer. You cannot tell if
it is devotion or science or the space between.
The grass listens harder than either of you.
Later, you will wonder if the field was learning
to pray from you, or teaching you to grow.

exits.label: where the mutation spreads like grammar
back to where the prayer was still prayer
upward where the words still scatter like birds
